title: Molecular insights into the interaction between human nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase and Toll-like receptor 4.
authors: Gasparrini, Massimiliano; Mazzola, Francesca; Cuccioloni, Massimiliano; Sorci, Leonardo; Audrito, Valentina; Zamporlini, Federica; Fortunato, Carlo; Amici, Adolfo; Cianci, Michele; Deaglio, Silvia; Angeletti, Mauro; Raffaelli, Nadia
one_liner_zh: 该文结合生物信息学、突变实验与分子对接研究人NAMPT与TLR4的蛋白-蛋白互作，虽非TF-DNA体系，但蛋白-蛋白结合界面建模与对接方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究，故给予中档评分。
abstract: The secreted form of the enzyme nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), which catalyzes a key reaction in intracellular NAD biosynthesis, acts as a damage-associated molecular pattern triggering Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated inflammatory responses. However, the precise mechanism of interaction is unclear. Using an integrated approach combining bioinformatics and functional and structural analyses, we investigated the interaction between NAMPT and TLR4 at the molecular level. Starting from previous evidence that the bacterial ortholog of NAMPT cannot elicit the inflammatory response, despite a high degree of structural conservation, two positively charged areas unique to the human enzyme (the alpha1-alpha2 and beta1-beta2 loops) were identified as likely candidates for TLR4 binding. However, alanine substitution of the positively charged residues within these loops did not affect either the oligomeric state or the catalytic efficiency of the enzyme. The kinetics of the binding of wildtype and mutated NAMPT to biosensor-tethered TLR4 was analyzed. We found that mutations in the alpha1-alpha2 loop strongly decreased the association rate, increasing the K(D) value from 18 nM, as determined for the wildtype, to 1.3 muM. In addition, mutations in the beta1-beta2 loop or its deletion increased the dissociation rate, yielding K(D) values of 0.63 and 0.22 muM, respectively. Mutations also impaired the ability of NAMPT to trigger the NF-kappaB inflammatory signaling pathway in human cultured macrophages. Finally, the involvement of the two loops in receptor binding was supported by NAMPT-TLR4 docking simulations. This study paves the way for future development of compounds that selectively target eNAMPT/TLR4 signaling in inflammatory disorders.
abstract_zh: 分泌形式的烟酰胺磷酸核糖转移酶（NAMPT）催化细胞内NAD生物合成中的关键反应，同时作为损伤相关分子模式，触发Toll样受体4（TLR4）介导的炎症反应。然而，其相互作用的精确机制尚不清楚。我们采用结合生物信息学、功能与结构分析的综合方法，在分子水平上研究了NAMPT与TLR4之间的相互作用。基于先前证据，即NAMPT的细菌同源物尽管结构高度保守，却无法引发炎症反应，我们鉴定出人类酶特有的两个正电荷区域（alpha1-alpha2和beta1-beta2环）为TLR4结合的潜在候选位点。然而，这些环内正电荷残基的丙氨酸替换并未影响酶的寡聚状态或催化效率。我们分析了野生型和突变型NAMPT与生物传感器固定的TLR4结合的动力学。结果发现，alpha1-alpha2环中的突变显著降低了结合速率，使K(D)值从野生型测得的18 nM增加至1.3 μM。此外，beta1-beta2环中的突变或其缺失增加了解离速率，分别产生0.63 μM和0.22 μM的K(D)值。突变还损害了NAMPT在人类培养巨噬细胞中触发NF-κB炎症信号通路的能力。最后，NAMPT-TLR4对接模拟支持了这两个环参与受体结合。本研究为未来开发选择性靶向炎症性疾病中eNAMPT/TLR4信号通路的化合物铺平了道路。
